messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high error rate for /v1/generate across hosted customers (slo: 99.9%). Alert: spike in 5xx from routing layer at 1954320998.
Emily: seeing it too. Latency +5xx up across multiple regions. All hosted tenants are getting degraded responses.
Sam: quick sanity — is this a model/kernel issue or routing? I see a bunch of policy logs showing fallback decisions.
Maya: pulling routing policy logs now. suspect: capacity-tier spillover rule fired even though dedicated pools are at zero claim capacity. Might be mis-evaluating "compatible_variants" set.
Priya: customer-impact: CS dashboard shows ~1200 failed requests in the last 10m from three mid-market customers. I've DM'd account owners.
Emily: can someone share the routing decision trace for a failed request id=rcpt-8f2b?
Infra Bot: trace for rcpt-8f2b: 
```
route_evaluate start
policy=capacity-tier-blend v=3.2
tenant=acme-corp
hosted_quota=unlimited
dedicated_claim=0
compatible_variants=[redwood/7b, redwood/7b-quant]
chosen_pool=dedicated-us-west-2-0
fallback_to=hosted-us-east-1
reason=spillover_to_dedicated
route_evaluate end
error=pool_unavailable
```
Sam: that log shows it explicitly picked a dedicated pool that has claim=0. That explains the loop: dedicated pool is unavailable -> fallback to hosted -> routing policy tries again and picks same dedicated pool due to stale topology state.
Maya: I can reproduce locally with the policy simulator. There's a precedence bug: when dedicated_claim==0 we should treat as not_candidate, but code path still marks it candidate if "prefer_dedicated" flag is true and tenant has reserved capacity flag.
Emily: mitigation plan? We need a fast control to stop host->dedicated spillover while we fix policy logic.
Priya: recommend temporary policy override: set prefer_dedicated=false globally for hosted routing. That should stop attempts to send new requests to dedicated pools. Also set tenant isolation hard-stop for affected tenants.
Sam: agree. Who can push override? Jordan can patch control plane policy in 2m. @Jordan?
Jordan: I'm on it. Pushing a soft override now: 
```
PATCH /control/policy/active
payload={"capacity_tier.prefer_dedicated":false, "spillover.enabled":false}
```
Jordan: applied override at 1954321302.
Oncall Bot: Incident annotation: override applied by Jordan at 1954321302.
Emily: after override, error rate dropped ~70% in the next 90s. Metrics: 5xx from routing layer down from 12% -> 3.5%.
CS Bot: Notifying impacted customers that we've applied mitigations and are investigating root cause. Template message queued.
Maya: I'm preparing a fix PR to patch the precedence check. Root cause: boolean evaluation of reserved_capacity flag combined with prefer_dedicated leading to candidate inclusion even when pool claim==0. Will add unit + integration tests in policy simulator.
Sam: we should also add a safety check in runtime: never pick pool if available_capacity < min_required_capacity. That'd have caught this. Can we push a small runtime guard as hotfix?
Jordan: I can push a hotfix to the routing runtime queue. Small guard, tested w/ canary in us-west-2 only. Will schedule canary in 10m.
Emily: also capture the loop timeline for postmortem: sequence of spillover decisions and the fallback bounce. We should include KL logs and the policy simulator run.
Maya: PR 3142 created: fix/preference-precedence. Description: treat dedicated_claim==0 as non-candidate unless explicit override is set. Tests added.
Sam: Jordan, what's the plan for canary and rollout?
Jordan: canary started at 1954322000 in us-west-2 (10% traffic). Monitoring hooks in console show no increase in errors, routing decisions now ignore zero-claim pools. Rolling to 50% in 5m if green.
Infra Bot: canary metrics: routing 5xx stable, latency unchanged.
Priya: CS asked for ETA on full resolution — we should estimate 90 mins to roll full fix + follow-up checks.
Emily: agree. We'll keep override until rollout complete and then remove override. Also schedule a lock to prevent automatic re-enable of spillover for 2 hours post-rollout.
Maya: follow-up tasks: postmortem, add guard in runtime (Sam + Jordan), add end-to-end test in policy simulator, alert adaptions to detect repeated bounce patterns. I'll own postmortem.
Sam: I'll file an ops ticket to change the safety threshold configuration and add a regression test.
CS Bot: Sent update to customers at 1954322105: "We applied a mitigation to routing policies to stop requests from being routed to unavailable dedicated pools. We're rolling a fix and will follow up with a detailed postmortem."
Emily: thanks all. Any outstanding asks?
Priya: please capture which tenants were impacted and include account IDs in the postmortem. I have a list and will attach.
Jordan: override removal scheduled for 1954323600 after full rollout verification.
Oncall Bot: Incident status: mitigated (override + canary pass). Assigning postmortem to Maya. Priority: P2 -> P3 after mitigation.
Maya: logging final actions and will start the postmortem doc. Will include timeline, diffs for PR 3142, and new tests.
Emily: closing the live incident channel in 30m, keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
